## Codebase Intelligence for OpenPower (Repowise)

Last indexed: 2026-11-05 (commit 5f2fc18).

### Architecture
OpenPower Engine consumes a player’s commands, world data, and versioned module definitions, then runs an authoritative simulation and presents the resulting world through an interactive client. Its pipeline loads and migrates mod-layered data, advances deterministic fixed-step simulation systems, records events and state, and produces snapshots for the UI, persisted saves, and replayable debugging. The project combines several distinct views of the same simulation. The asynchronous multi-process core keeps the UI separate from the authoritative simulation and exchanges acknowledged Arrow IPC snapshots with table-level deltas.

### Key modules
- `src/client/ui`: UI code takes shared state and services and draws the screens people use to inspect and change the game
- `modules`: Modules hold the game’s domain systems and supporting policies
- `src/shared`: Shared actions, commands, configuration, advisor settings, covert options, and determinism define common rules that client and server code…
- `modules/base/systems`: These systems handle shared world state and the rules that shape it
- `src/client/ui/core`: This part provides shared ways to compose interface elements, manage windows, apply visual styling, load fonts, and draw common widgets
- `modules/base/systems/military`: This part defines military capabilities, battle strategy, alliances, authority, and related military policies while leaving their user…
- `src/client/ui/components`: UI code builds the menus, dialogs, windows, and heads-up display that the client shows as players interact with the game
- `modules/base/systems/world`: This part handles diplomatic relations and treaties, authority checks, annexation, and advice for country decisions
- `src/client/ui/panels/military`: These panels let players inspect battles, compare forces, read battle maps, and view military information
- `src/client/ui/components/shared`: Reusable dialogs collect choices, show outcomes, and confirm actions across battles, campaigns, profiles, covert operations, and close…

### How to work in this repo

- **Pre-edit, not instead-of-edit.** These tools decide *which* files to read and edit. Claude Code requires a raw Read of any file you will Edit, and that Read is correct and expected. Bytes marked `verified: true` need no re-read; re-read only what `bounds: "approximate"` names. An empty `callers`/`used_by` comes with a `*_basis`: read it before concluding nothing calls a symbol.
- **Noisy commands** (tests, builds, `git log`/`diff`): prefer `repowise distill <cmd>`, same exit code, errors first. Recover a `[repowise#<ref>: N lines omitted]` marker with `repowise expand <ref>` (`-q <regex>` filters); never re-run the command.
- **Record a decision** you reasoned out: `repowise decision add --agent <your slug> --title T --decision D --rationale '<why>' --affects <path>` (lands as a candidate; accept candidates with `repowise decision confirm <id> --agent <your slug> --evidence <commit|file>`).

### Tools

| Tool | When and why |
|------|--------------|
| `get_answer(question)` | First call for any how/where/why question. Cite `confidence: "high"` or `grounding: "extracted"` directly; `degraded` means no prose; `confidence` rates the evidence. `symbol_bodies` has live bodies. |
| `get_context(targets=[...])` | Triage card for files/modules/symbols: docs, signatures, hotspot, fix history. No source bytes — `include=["skeleton"]` for the whole file verified, `["callers"|"decisions"]` for depth. Batch targets. |
| `get_symbol(id, depth?)` | **Follow-up, not an entry point** — one verified body for an id a prior response named (`path.py::Name`, `path.py:140-180`, `repowise#<hex>`). Never walk a file symbol by symbol; Read it. |
| `search_codebase(query)` | Hybrid search, auto-routed by query shape; force with `mode=symbol|path|concept|hybrid`. A hit whose `sources` are `[fts]` only has no semantic agreement, so verify it. |
| `get_why(query, targets?)` | Why the code is shaped this way: decision records, git archaeology, rationale comments. Call before a refactor or a pattern divergence. |
| `get_risk(targets?, changed_files?, include?)` | File history and structural reach. PR mode leads with `directive`; its 0-10 structural heuristic is uncalibrated, not a probability. Read typed test recommendations and coverage state first. |
| `get_change_risk(revspec?, extensions?, exclude_patterns?)` | Deterministic live-diff review signal for a commit or range. Lead with benchmarked percentile/classification; the 0-10 diff-shape score is supporting, not a probability. `get_risk` scores paths. |
| `get_health(targets?, include?)` | Defect / maintainability / performance scores and findings, plus documentation the code no longer supports. Self-check the files you touched before finishing. |
| `get_dead_code(tier?, min_confidence?, safe_only?)` | Confidence-tiered unreachable files / unused exports / zombie packages. For cleanup sweeps, not targeted fixes. |
| `get_overview()` | Architecture map. Call once, first, in an unfamiliar repo; skip it after that. |
